seo.h1: Does Steak 'n Shake Fry in Beef Tallow?

question: Does Steak 'n Shake Fry in Beef Tallow?
quick_answer: Yes. Steak 'n Shake switched from vegetable oil to 100% beef tallow for its shoestring fries at all of its roughly 400 U.S. restaurants by early 2025, and later used tallow for its onion rings and chicken tenders too. Beef tallow is rendered beef fat, so the fries are no longer vegetarian.
key_facts: Announced January 16, 2025; all locations switched by about March 1, 2025
Fries, onion rings and chicken tenders are cooked in beef tallow
Steak 'n Shake was the first major chain to switch back to tallow

body.heading: What changed at Steak 'n Shake
body.text: On January 16, 2025, Steak 'n Shake announced it would fry its shoestring fries in 100% all-natural beef tallow instead of vegetable oil. The switch rolled out state by state and reached all locations around March 1, 2025. By late March, the chain said its fries, onion rings and chicken tenders were all cooked in tallow. Its menu now calls them Beef Tallow Fries.

body.heading: What beef tallow is
body.text: Beef tallow is fat rendered from beef. It is solid at room temperature, a bit like butter, and handles high frying temperatures well. Fast-food chains used it widely until around 1990, when McDonald's and others moved to vegetable oil amid concern about saturated fat. Tallow has more saturated fat than oils like canola or peanut oil, which is also what gives fries a richer flavor.

body.heading: Why Steak 'n Shake switched
body.text: Steak 'n Shake said it wanted the best-tasting, most authentic fries, noting that the earliest fries were cooked in tallow. Executives said the company had wanted to switch for years but needed a supplier that could provide additive-free tallow at scale. The move came as Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was urging restaurants to drop seed oils, and the chain promoted the change with a nod to him. Health groups such as the American Heart Association say there is no reason to avoid seed oils, so the health debate is far from settled.

body.heading: Are the fries vegetarian?
body.text: No. Because they are fried in beef fat, Steak 'n Shake's fries, onion rings and tenders are not vegetarian or vegan. The company has said plainly that vegetarians should look elsewhere for fries.

body.heading: Other chains that use beef tallow
body.text: Steak 'n Shake was the first big chain to switch back, but some others already used tallow for at least some fried foods, including Buffalo Wild Wings and Outback Steakhouse. Smaller chains like Fry the Coop and Burger Boss have built their menus around it too. For Steak 'n Shake's prices, including the fries, see our Steak 'n Shake menu page.
